meta.title: SF Adventures
meta.description: A catalog of San Francisco adventures for two. Source of truth for the app.

schema.name: display name
schema.neighborhood: SF area, for clustering nearby activities
schema.description: why it's a fun adventure for two

logistics.gettingThere: transit/parking note

pairsWith: ids of nearby activities that combine well

activities.name: Lands End Coastal Trail
activities.description: A cliffside trail with cypress groves, hidden coves, and dead-on Golden Gate Bridge views. Start at the Sutro Baths ruins and wander to Mile Rock Beach and the stone labyrinth out on the point.

logistics.gettingThere: Parking lot at Merrie Way; Muni 38 to 48th Ave. Bring a windbreaker — it's foggy and cold.

activities.name: Sutro Baths Ruins & Cliff House
activities.description: Explore the concrete skeleton of a giant Victorian bathhouse right on the surf, then duck into the sea cave at the far end when the tide's low.

logistics.gettingThere: Same lot as Lands End. Sturdy shoes — rocks are slick.

activities.name: Twin Peaks at Sunset
activities.description: The best 360° view in the city — downtown, the bay, the bridges, the ocean, all at once. Time it for golden hour and stay as the fog rolls in and the lights come on.

logistics.gettingThere: Drive or bike up Twin Peaks Blvd; small lot at the top. Windy and cold — bring layers.

activities.name: 16th Ave Tiled Steps + Grand View Park
activities.description: Climb a 163-step mosaic staircase (sea to stars), then keep going up to Grand View Park (Turtle Hill) for a surprise panorama of the ocean and the whole west side.

logistics.gettingThere: 16th Ave & Moraga. Muni N to Sunset. It's a real stair workout.

activities.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops Picnic
activities.description: New parkland built over the highway tunnels with lawns, overlooks, and campfire-style seating framing the Golden Gate Bridge. Grab food from the Presidio Pop-Up nearby and picnic.

logistics.gettingThere: Free Presidio Go shuttle; parking at the Presidio Transit Center.

activities.name: Andy Goldsworthy Sculpture Hunt
activities.description: Four hidden land-art installations scattered through the Presidio forest — Spire, Wood Line, Tree Fall, and Earth Wall. Make a scavenger hunt of finding all four on foot.

logistics.gettingThere: Start near the Presidio main post; map the four locations first.

activities.name: Crissy Field to Warming Hut Walk
activities.description: Flat waterfront stroll from the Marina out to Torpedo Wharf (best under-the-bridge view in the city) and the Warming Hut café. Watch kite-surfers and container ships slide by.

logistics.gettingThere: Parking along Mason St; PresidiGo shuttle. Coffee/snacks at the Warming Hut.

activities.name: Corona Heights Park
activities.description: A short scramble up a red-rock outcrop rewards you with a clear downtown-and-bay view and way fewer tourists than Twin Peaks. The Randall Museum at the base is a fun add-on.

logistics.gettingThere: States St & Museum Way. Street parking; steep in spots.

activities.name: Angel Island Day Trip
activities.neighborhood: SF Bay (ferry from the Ferry Building)
activities.description: Ferry to the 'Ellis Island of the West,' then bike or hike the 5-mile perimeter road for 360° bay views, immigration-station history, and a picnic with no cars in sight.

logistics.gettingThere: Blue & Gold ferry from Pier 41 or the Ferry Building; book ahead on weekends. Bike rentals on the island.

activities.name: Ocean Beach Bonfire
activities.description: Claim one of the designated concrete fire rings, bring firewood and s'mores, and watch the sun drop into the Pacific. The quintessential low-key SF evening.

logistics.gettingThere: Fire rings near Fulton–Lincoln. Fires allowed until 9:30pm, must use the rings. Bring layers, it gets cold fast.

activities.name: Bernal Heights Hilltop
activities.description: A grassy, off-leash-friendly hill with a mellow loop trail and one of the coziest city panoramas. Locals-and-their-dogs energy, especially at sunset.

logistics.gettingThere: Bernal Heights Blvd loops the hill; street parking below.

activities.name: Stow Lake Pedal Boats
activities.description: Rent a pedal or row boat and drift around Strawberry Hill, past the waterfall and Chinese pavilion. Ridiculously charming and cheap. Cap it with the boathouse snack bar.

logistics.gettingThere: Stow Lake Boathouse, Golden Gate Park. Cash or card; hourly rentals.

activities.name: Japanese Tea Garden
activities.description: The oldest public Japanese garden in the US — koi ponds, a drum bridge, pagodas, and a tea house for matcha and mochi. Go right at opening on a weekday for near-solitude (free before 10am on some mornings).

logistics.gettingThere: Music Concourse, Golden Gate Park. Free entry early on Mon/Wed/Fri mornings — check current hours.

activities.name: Glen Canyon Park
activities.description: A genuinely wild rocky canyon hidden in the middle of the city — a creek, red-tailed hawks, and beginner rock-climbing outcrops. Feels like you left SF entirely.

logistics.gettingThere: Glen Park BART, then a short walk; or park at Elk & Chenery.

activities.name: Ferry Building Marketplace + Farmers Market
activities.description: Graze your way through artisan stalls — oysters at Hog Island, Cowgirl cheese, Blue Bottle, Recchiuti chocolates. Come Saturday morning for the huge waterfront farmers market.

logistics.gettingThere: Embarcadero BART/Muni; the F-line streetcar drops you at the door. Farmers market Tue/Thu/Sat.

activities.name: Swan Oyster Depot
activities.description: A century-old seafood counter with 18 stools and no tables. Sit elbow-to-elbow, order the combo crab-and-oyster plate, and chat with the fishmongers. A true SF rite of passage.

logistics.gettingThere: 1517 Polk St. Cash preferred, counter only, expect a line — go early or off-peak.

activities.name: Mission Burrito Showdown
activities.description: Settle the eternal debate for yourselves: split a carnitas super burrito at La Taqueria (no rice, sued into being 'America's best') vs. El Farolito at midnight. Deeply serious, deeply fun.

logistics.gettingThere: 24th St BART for La Taqueria; both are cash-friendly. Bring an appetite.

activities.name: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
activities.description: A gloriously kitschy tiki bar in the Fairmont basement with an indoor lagoon, a floating band, and a simulated thunderstorm every 30 minutes. Order a scorpion bowl and lean into it.

logistics.gettingThere: Fairmont Hotel, 950 Mason St. Cable car up California St for the full effect. Book ahead on weekends.

activities.name: Cocktails at Trick Dog
activities.description: A world's-best-bars regular that reinvents its whole themed menu a couple times a year (a Zodiac, a Pantone deck, a mixtape). Inventive drinks, great snacks, buzzy upstairs.

logistics.gettingThere: 3010 20th St. No reservations — go early or expect a wait upstairs.

activities.name: Chinatown Dim Sum
activities.description: Grab a box of pillowy pork buns and shrimp har gow to-go from Good Mong Kok, then eat them on a Portsmouth Square bench, or sit down for the full cart experience elsewhere.

logistics.gettingThere: Stockton St. Cash for the to-go spots; wander Ross Alley and the fortune-cookie factory after.

activities.name: Off the Grid: Fort Mason (Fridays)
activities.description: SF's biggest food-truck gathering — 30+ trucks, a bar, and live music on the waterfront on Friday nights (seasonal). Graze small plates from a dozen cuisines with the bridge in view.

logistics.gettingThere: Fort Mason Center. Friday evenings, roughly spring–fall — check the schedule.

activities.name: Bi-Rite Creamery + Dolores Park
activities.description: Get salted-caramel or honey-lavender scoops (or the soft-serve window to skip the line), then find a patch of grass at Dolores Park for peak sunny-day people-watching and skyline views.

logistics.gettingThere: 18th & Dolores. The scoop-shop line can be long; the soft-serve window next door is faster.

activities.name: Outer Sunset Coffee Crawl
activities.description: Warm up with a Snowy Plover (espresso, sparkling water, cream) at Andytown, then wander the sleepy surf-town blocks of Judah St to more cafés, thrift shops, and the beach.

logistics.gettingThere: Muni N to the outer stops. Foggy and mellow — a cozy morning.

activities.name: Dogpatch / SoMa Brewery Hop
activities.description: Work through a few beloved indie taprooms — Cellarmaker, Harmonic, or Triple Voodoo — often with a food truck parked outside and shuffleboard inside. Laid-back afternoon energy.

logistics.gettingThere: T-Third light rail through Dogpatch. Many taprooms are dog-friendly.

activities.name: de Young Museum + Free Tower
activities.description: American art and blockbuster shows in a striking copper building — but the sleeper move is the free glass observation tower on the 9th floor for a 360° view over the park and city.

logistics.gettingThere: Music Concourse, Golden Gate Park. Tower is free even without a ticket. Free admission on the first Tuesday monthly.

activities.name: California Academy of Sciences (NightLife 21+)
activities.description: A rainforest dome, planetarium, aquarium, and living roof under one ceiling. Thursday's 21+ NightLife turns it into a cocktails-and-science party with DJs — a genuinely great date.

logistics.gettingThere: Across the concourse from the de Young. NightLife is Thursdays 6–10pm, 21+; book online.

activities.name: Exploratorium After Dark (18+)
activities.description: A hands-on science playground for grown-ups on Thursday nights — hundreds of tinker-with-it exhibits, a Tactile Dome, cocktails, and a rotating adult theme. Endlessly playful.

logistics.gettingThere: Pier 15 on the Embarcadero; F-line streetcar. After Dark is Thursdays 6–10pm, 18+.

activities.name: SFMOMA
activities.description: Seven floors of modern and contemporary art, a free-to-visit second-floor sculpture terrace and living wall, and a rooftop garden. Big, contemplative, and easy to pair with dinner downtown.

logistics.gettingThere: 151 Third St; Montgomery BART. The ground/second-floor galleries and terrace are free to enter.

activities.name: Legion of Honor
activities.description: A Beaux-Arts palace of European art (and a real Rodin Thinker) perched above the sea with a Golden Gate view from the front steps. Combine with a Lands End walk for the perfect day.

logistics.gettingThere: 100 34th Ave, Lincoln Park. Free admission first Tuesday monthly. Pairs perfectly with Lands End.

activities.name: Movie at the Castro / Roxie / Balboa
activities.description: See something on a real single-screen marquee — a sing-along, a restored classic, or a first-run indie — at one of SF's historic movie palaces. Old-school date magic.

logistics.gettingThere: Castro (Castro St), Roxie (16th St, Mission), Balboa (Outer Richmond). Note: the Castro Theatre is under renovation — check status.

activities.name: City Lights Books + North Beach Beat Walk
activities.description: Browse the legendary Beat-era bookstore, toast the poets at Vesuvio next door via Jack Kerouac Alley, then walk the espresso-and-focaccia blocks of North Beach.

logistics.gettingThere: 261 Columbus Ave. Pair with a cannoli from Stella and a bench in Washington Square.

activities.name: Live Music at The Chapel / GAMH / Fillmore
activities.description: Catch a show at one of SF's great mid-size rooms — The Chapel (a converted mortuary), the ornate Great American Music Hall, or the historic Fillmore (free apples and a poster on the way out).

logistics.gettingThere: Buy tickets in advance. The Chapel and GAMH have attached restaurants for dinner-and-a-show.

activities.name: Musée Mécanique
activities.description: A free-to-enter warehouse of 300+ working antique arcade machines — hand-cranked dioramas, fortune tellers, and old strength testers. Bring a roll of quarters and play everything.

logistics.gettingThere: Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf. Free entry; bring quarters (change machines on site).

activities.name: Kayaking Mission Creek / McCovey Cove
activities.description: Paddle a tandem kayak through the houseboat-lined channel and out toward the ballpark's McCovey Cove. Calm water, a totally different angle on the city, and resident harbor seals.

logistics.gettingThere: City Kayak near the ballpark; T-Third to the stadium. Book tandem kayaks ahead.

activities.name: Bike the Golden Gate to Sausalito
activities.description: Rent bikes, ride across the Golden Gate Bridge, coast downhill into Sausalito for lunch and ice cream, then ferry back with the bikes as the sun sets. A perfect big-day loop.

logistics.gettingThere: Rentals near Fisherman's Wharf or the Marina. Reserve a bike-ferry spot back; it fills up.

activities.name: Urban Putt Indoor Mini Golf
activities.description: A dark, whimsical 14-hole indoor mini-golf course full of kinetic Rube-Goldberg contraptions, plus a full bar and restaurant. Competitive, silly, and great on a foggy night.

logistics.gettingThere: 1096 South Van Ness. Reserve a tee time on weekends; 21+ after certain hours.

activities.name: Roller Disco at Church of 8 Wheels
activities.description: Skate under disco lights inside a repurposed church with a DJ spinning funk and soul. Rentals available, zero skill required, maximum joy. Also: free 'Skatin' Place' in GG Park on Sundays.

logistics.gettingThere: 554 Fillmore St. Cash/card at the door; skate rentals included. Check nights/hours.

activities.name: Indoor Climbing at Dogpatch Boulders
activities.description: A big, friendly bouldering gym — no ropes, no experience needed. Belay-free climbing you can do side by side, then split a beer at a nearby taproom. Great rainy-day energy-burner.

logistics.gettingThere: 2573 Third St. Day pass + shoe rental for first-timers; T-Third light rail.

activities.name: Cable Car Ride + Lombard Street
activities.description: Hang off a rattling cable car up Hyde St, hop off to walk down the flower-lined crooked block of Lombard, and take in the bay-and-Alcatraz view from the top. Touristy on purpose, still a blast.

logistics.gettingThere: Powell-Hyde line. Buy a Muni day pass to skip the single-ride cost. Board at a mid-route stop to avoid the terminal line.

activities.name: Lindy in the Park (Free Swing Dancing)
activities.description: Free outdoor swing dancing every Sunday on JFK Drive, with a beginner lesson to start. No partner or experience needed — just show up and get spun around on a car-free promenade.

logistics.gettingThere: JFK Promenade near the de Young. Sundays ~11am–2pm; free lesson at the start.

activities.name: Emporium Arcade Bar
activities.description: A cavernous barcade with classic pinball, cabinet games, skee-ball, and a full bar. Load up a game card, get competitive, and settle scores over cocktails. Rainy-night proof.

logistics.gettingThere: 616 Divisadero (also a Mission location). 21+ in the evenings.

activities.name: Dolores Park Hang
activities.description: SF's ultimate sunny-day living room — bring a blanket, snacks, and drinks, claim a spot on the sloped lawn (the 'gay beach' side has the best sun and skyline view), and watch the whole city show up.

logistics.gettingThere: 18th & Dolores; J-Church stops at the park. Restrooms on site. Roving vendors sell drinks and treats.
